channel.title: Queering Earth — what has arrived
channel.description: Every page in the cabinet as it arrives — the sheets and the pages that are not sheets, newest first. The register's own accessions, including every correction, are a separate feed at https://queering.earth/register.xml. Generated from the pages themselves by tools/make-whats-new.mjs.

item.title: Every Day’s Most Quiet Need
item.description: Limerence read as monotropic attention rather than as a disorder — Glass, Beethoven, Huxley and García Márquez held against the line in Browning where a love poem stops climbing and comes down to the level of an ordinary day.

item.title: The plate
item.description: Every sheet on queering.earth in accession order, with what a sheet is, what a reading, an essay and a wall each mean, and what the numbers do and do not say.

item.title: My Gloomy Sunflowers
item.description: Townes Van Zandt, Vincent van Gogh, Sylvia Plath and Kurt Cobain, read against the myth that made them: four records in which the work was not the symptom but the thing that was going well.

item.title: The founding papers
item.description: The founding papers of queering.earth: the aims, the manifesto, and the paper about the shelf — what each is for, why none of them is a sheet, and which one is signed.

item.title: The cabinet itself
item.description: The working pages of queering.earth: the colophon, the register, the ledger, the decisions, the finding aid and the privacy page — what each is for, and what the build checks about them.

item.title: What has arrived, and when
item.description: Every page in the cabinet, newest first, with the day it arrived and how often it has been corrected since. The register says why something changed; this page says what is here. Subscribe by feed, or read the register at length.

item.title: What we quote, and why we may
item.description: This site’s fair-use position, written down: what we quote from work still in copyright, how much of it, why we think we may, and what to do if you hold the rights and disagree.

item.title: The Five Unmistakable Marks
item.description: Lewis Carroll's Snark, a creature named before anybody saw it; Deleuze's empty square; and Kassiane Asasumasu, who coined neurodivergent and had to say so out loud.

item.title: Other People Who Have It
item.description: Octavia Butler's hyperempathy, which Sami Schalk reads as a disability with no real-world equivalent, and the Autistic people who have been describing it under the same name for years.

item.title: Two Cohabitating Modes
item.description: Why this cabinet has a sibling built on science: the fox and the hedgehog from Archilochus to Berlin to Gould, two public-domain animal poems that end in the same place, and the spiky profile the typology was never written about.

item.title: The Preferred Flower of Life
item.description: Monotropa uniflora, the ghost pipe: a plant with no chlorophyll that feeds off fungi, the flower Emily Dickinson called the preferred flower of life, and the Greek root it shares with monotropism.

item.title: What this cabinet is for
item.description: The mission of queering.earth, in thirteen aims — each with the page where it is already being kept, and the failure that would show we had stopped. Then what a cabinet of readings has to do with a foundation whose first business is paying people's rent, including the half of that a reading cannot do.

item.title: Nothing here was inevitable
item.description: The manifesto of queering.earth: normal is an arrangement and arrangements have authors, weird is a verb, and a reading is where an arrangement gets contested. Adapted from the Neuroqueer Learning Spaces Manifesto under its own licence.

item.title: Find a word in the cabinet
item.description: Search every sheet, every quotation and every correction on this site. The searching happens in your browser; nothing you type is sent anywhere, including to us.

item.title: The attribution ledger
item.description: The ledger for every quotation and credited idea on Queering Earth: what we quoted, whose it is, where it came from, and the day somebody read the primary source and confirmed the wording. Including the ones we got wrong.

item.title: What is settled, and what is open
item.description: The decision log for Queering Earth: what is settled, what is still open, and the reasoning for each — including the designs that were refused, and why.

item.title: What this site knows about you
item.description: Almost nothing, and here is the whole of it: two view preferences your own browser keeps, and the server log our host writes. No analytics, no cookies, no forms, and one embedded recording that fetches nothing until you press play.

item.title: The Die Uncast
item.description: Christina Rossetti's Promises like Pie-crust, read as a charter for solo polyamory — the relationship escalator refused in 1861, and the colon her first printing keeps where everyone else prints a full stop.

item.title: Wyrd, Weird, and the Invention of Normal
item.description: Wyrd was Old English for fate. It became weird, and then weird became a diagnosis. A sheet on the demotion of a word, the Weird Sisters, changelings, refusal, and an idea of normal barely two centuries old.

item.title: Miranda: To Be Wondered With
item.description: Shakespeare coined Miranda's name from the Latin for wonder at. A reading of The Tempest and Waterhouse's 1916 canvas: a boy actor, an editor who moved her hardest speech into her father's mouth, and who a story lets be difficult.

item.title: The Swell and the Dwell
item.description: Emily Dickinson's Wild nights – Wild nights! read as co-regulation: the winds futile rather than stilled, the compass and the chart put down, and one night asked for instead of a lifetime. With a reply in verse, and what her first editor tidied in 1891.

item.title: A Waste Garden, Flowering at Its Will
item.description: Violet, pansy, green carnation, and lavender were worn as code. Each was read by the people it was meant to escape and turned into the word that named you, and each was picked up again afterwards. With the 1926 sentence about a streak of lavender, and the man it is actually about.

item.title: The accession register
item.description: The changelog for Queering Earth: every sheet as it was mounted, every plate that came off again, and every label we corrected — including the attributions we got wrong and exactly how they were fixed.

item.title: The Army of the Upright
item.description: Virginia Woolf's On Being Ill, mounted as she left it in 1930. Illness missing from literature, a language that runs dry, and the sentence she revised into something stranger.

item.title: Coming to Terms
item.description: Ryan Boren on a lifetime of not fitting gender norms, a pair of pink-tinted glasses, and the two words — autigender and neuroqueer — that finally fit.

item.title: Queering Earth
item.description: Reading the world through a queering lens — art, literature, poetry, politics, people, history — and asking what else any of it could have been. A Stimpunks Foundation and More Realms collaboration.

item.title: How this site is made
item.description: The design of Queering Earth: a Victorian herbarium sheet as the model, biophilic ground rules, the palette, the type, the drawings, and what we mean by specimen, sheet, plate, and label.
